# Vigil Journal: Critical Testing Insights

## 2026-10-02 - Deterministic AlertEngine and Flow Canonicalization Testing
**Challenge:** Alert messages generated by `AlertEngine` format flow endpoints based on `FlowKey`. Because `FlowKey::new` / `FlowKey::aggregate` canonicalizes IP addresses such that endpoint `a <= b`, assertions expecting endpoint order to mirror packet `(src, dst)` arguments can fail. Furthermore, time-dependent rate and PPS evaluations require synthetic `Instant` timelines with explicit delta durations (`dt >= 0.001s`) to avoid division by zero or non-deterministic rate window degradation.
**Strategy:** Structure test cases by controlling synthetic time offsets (`t0 + Duration::from_secs(...)`) and anticipating the canonicalized endpoint ordering (`a <= b`) in `AlertEngine` messages. For PPS testing, pass two successive evaluation frames with known packet count deltas to verify exact threshold trigger boundaries.
**Prevention:** Always assert canonicalized endpoint representations (`f.key.a \u{2194} f.key.b`) and feed controlled `Instant` progression rather than relying on real elapsed system time.
